### Changed
- **The serving slice's llm-d images come from the `llm-d-fast/` prefix, and the pre-pull names that image** (giantswarm/agent-platform#568). The well-known `LLMInferenceServiceConfig`s and the pre-pull DaemonSet named the runtime image as mirrored byte-identically, `gsoci.azurecr.io/giantswarm/llm-d-cuda:v0.8.0` — 8.2 GiB compressed in gzip layers of 5.5, 1.4 and 1.0 GB. containerd pulls one HTTPS stream per layer, so the stream carrying the 5.5 GB layer bounded the pull: about 60 MB/s effective, 132–149 s on a fresh pool node where one stream measures 95 MB/s and four 306 MB/s, and the operands pulled beside it ran three to five times slower meanwhile — with the pre-pull in place, the longest cold-start step left. giantswarm/llm-d publishes the same images re-layered under `llm-d-fast/` of the same registry path (zstd, `llm-d-cuda` split into layers of at most 1.2 GB). The meta chart's `kserve-runtime-configs:` block now passes `kserve.llmisvcConfigs.imageRegistry: gsoci.azurecr.io/giantswarm/llm-d-fast/`, so every reference the configs render carries the prefix, and `modelServing.prepull.images` defaults to `gsoci.azurecr.io/giantswarm/llm-d-fast/llm-d-cuda:v0.8.0` in both charts, so the pre-pull warms exactly the image the predictor runs. Going back is two values: the block's `imageRegistry` at `gsoci.azurecr.io/giantswarm/` (the byte-identical mirror) or `ghcr.io/llm-d/` (upstream), and the matching reference in `prepull.images`. `make verify-serving-slice` asserts the prefix on the rendered release and that the pre-pull's reference carries it; `verify-gpu-pool` leaves the pre-pull DaemonSet out of the golden comparison while `origin/main` names the mirror's image. README "The well-known configs" and "Pre-pulling the runtime image"; UPGRADE.md.
